subject: Business Models
title: Unit Economics Always Win
description: Learn Unit Economics Always Win in one minute.

hook.text: Pets.com, Kozmo, Webvan, MoviePass—each lost money on every transaction and assumed scale would fix it.

buildup.text: Unit economics measure profit or loss per transaction. If each sale loses money, more sales means more losses.

discovery.text: Venture capital can subsidize losses temporarily, but eventually investors want returns. Cash runs out.

twist.text: Amazon lost money for years too—but its unit economics improved as it scaled. The trajectory mattered, not the snapshot.

climax.text: The question isn't 'profitable today?' It's 'do unit economics improve per sale?' Scale won't fix bad math.

punchline.text: Lose $1 per sale, sell a million. That's a million-dollar loss, not a business.

quiz.question: When can negative unit economics be acceptable?
options: When unit economics improve with scale and trajectory is clear
Always, if you have VC funding

details.summary: Unit economics measure the direct revenues and costs of a single transaction or customer. Businesses that lose money on each transaction cannot achieve profitability through scale alone. Growth only amplifies losses when the fundamental unit economic equation is negative.
details.whyItMatters: Every failed startup in this course ignored unit economics. Pets.com, MoviePass, Kozmo, and WeWork all believed scale would solve negative unit economics. It never does. This lesson is the most important in all of business model analysis.
takeaways: Unit economics measure profit or loss on each individual transaction
Negative unit economics cannot be fixed by growth, which only amplifies losses
Every iconic startup failure in this course ignored this fundamental principle

faq.question: What are the key components of unit economics?
faq.answer: Revenue per unit (price paid per transaction or customer), variable costs per unit (direct costs of fulfilling that transaction), and contribution margin (revenue minus variable costs). Customer acquisition cost and lifetime value complete the picture at the customer level.

faq.question: When is it acceptable to have temporarily negative unit economics?
faq.answer: Only when there is a concrete, testable path to positive unit economics at specific scale thresholds. Network effects that reduce costs, volume discounts from suppliers, or technology improvements that lower marginal costs must be demonstrable, not theoretical.
